newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease, seen declining further.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease, seen declining further.

text.p: Slovenia's blue chip SBI index eased 1.5 percent on Tuesday in what traders described as a technical correction to recent strong gains.
Market participants said international investors were waiting for prices to stabilise and forecast the retracement could continue on Wednesday.
The SBI index has risen by a total of 7.7 percent over the last seven trading days.
"Foreign investors are buying smart in order to prevent prices rising too fast," one trader said.
The SBI index fell 23.79 points to 1,558.40. Dealers forecast short-term losses would not exceed another 25 points.
Overall 12 shares fell, four rose, two were unchanged and ten were untraded. Turnover rose to 170.7 million tolars from 156.3 million.
Petrol trader Petrol was most actively traded. Its shares fell 1.64 percent to 24,640 tolars on volume of 3,649 shares.
Traders said Petrol was unlikely to fall below 24,500 tolars as international interest in the company, which is the second largest in the country, remained strong.
Preferred shares of Kovinotehna led the decliners, down 9.07 percent to 491 on volume of 3,390 shares.
Construction company GPG was the top gainer, up 9.09 percent to 6,000 tolars on volume of 20 shares. Traders said the share was experiencing a rebound after a fall of 5.17 percent on Monday.
